questions.question: Consider a long solenoid of length $I$ and radius $r$. If $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space, the inductance of the solenoid is :
questions.explanation:
Self-inductance of solenoid

\[\begin{aligned} & L=\frac{N \phi}{i} \\ & L=\frac{N B A}{i} \\ & L=\frac{N \mu_0 n i A}{i}[n=\frac{N}{I}] \\ & L=N \mu_0 n A \\ & L=(\frac{N}{I}) \mu_0 n A I \\ & L=\mu_0 n^2 A I \\ & L=\mu_0 n^2 \pi r^2 I[\because A=\pi r^2] \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
Two identical inductors are connected in two different configurations $P$ and $Q$, where a time varying current $l(t)$ is flowing, as shown in the figure. The induced emf between points $a$ and $b$ for configuration $P$ is $E_P$ and that for configuration $Q$ is $E_Q$. The ratio $E_P / E_Q$ is:

[Neglect the effect of mutual inductance.]
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} &\text { In figure }(P)\\ &E_P=E_{a b}=-\frac{L d I(t)}{d t} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,...(i)\end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} &\text { In figure (Q) }\\ &E_Q=E_{a b}=-\frac{L}{2} \frac{d I(t)}{d t} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,...(ii)\end{aligned}\]

\[\Rightarrow \frac{E_P}{E_Q}=\frac{2}{1}\]

questions.question: A conducting loop of finite resistance lies on the $x-y$ plane. There is a constant magnetic field in the $z$ direction. The area of the loop varies with time $t$, as $A=A_0(1+\sin t)$ in appropriate units. The figure that correctly indicates the qualitative behaviour of the power $P$ dissipated in the loop as a function of time is:
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} &\text { } A=A_0(1+\sin t)\\ &\begin{aligned} & \phi=B A=B A_0(1+\sin t) \\ & \varepsilon=-\frac{d \phi}{d t}=-B A_0 \cos t \\ & I_{\text {induced }}=\frac{\varepsilon_{\text {ind }}}{R}=-\frac{B A_0}{R} \cos t \\ & \text { Power }=P=I^2 R=\frac{B^2 A_0^2 \cos ^2 t}{R} \\ & P \propto \cos ^2 t \end{aligned} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: A rectangular wire loop of sides 8 cm and 3 cm with a small cut, is moving out of a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.3 T directed normal to the plane of the loop. The emf developed across the cut, if the velocity of the loop is $2 \mathrm{~cm} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$, in a direction normal to the shorter side of the loop, will be :
questions.explanation:
Induced emf across the shorter side

\[\begin{aligned} & E_{\text {induced }}=B V l[\because \vec{B} \perp \vec{V} \perp \vec{I}] \\ & =0.3 \times 2 \times 10^{-2} \times 3 \times 10^{-2} \\ & =1.8 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~V} \\ & =1.8 \times 10^{-4} \text { volt } \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: $A B$ is a part of an electrical circuit (see figure). The potential difference " $V_A-V_B$ ", at the instant when current $i=2 \mathrm{~A}$ and is increasing at a rate of $1 \mathrm{amp} /$ second is:
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} &\text { Given, } l=2 \mathrm{~A} \text { and } \frac{d i}{d t}=+1 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{s}\\ &\begin{aligned} & V_A-L \frac{d i}{d t}-5-i \times 2=V_B \\ & \Rightarrow V_A-1 \times 1-5-2 \times 2=V_B \\ & \Rightarrow V_A-V_B=10 \text { volt } \end{aligned} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: Let us consider two solenoids \(A\) and \(B\), made from same magnetic material of relative permeability \(\mu_r\) and equal area of cross-section. Length of \(A\) is twice that of \(B\) and the number of turns per unit length in \(A\) is half that of \(B\). The ratio of self inductances of the two solenoids, \(L_A: L_B\) is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} & L=\mu_0 \mu_r \times n \times A \times N \\ & L=\mu_0 \mu_r n \times A \times \frac{N}{I} \times I \\ & L=\mu_0 \mu_r \times n^2 \times A \times I \Rightarrow L \propto n^2 I \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{L_A}{L_B}=\frac{n_A^2}{n_B^2} \times \frac{I_A}{I_B} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{L_A}{L_B}=\frac{1}{4} \times 2=\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: An emf is generated by an ac generator having 100 turn coil, of loop area \(1 \mathrm{~m}^2\). The coil rotates at a speed of one revolution per second and placed in a uniform magnetic field of \(0.05 \mathrm{~T}\) perpendicular to the axis of rotation of the coil. The maximum value of emf is :-
questions.explanation:
\[\omega=2\pi \frac{\mathrm{rad}}{\mathrm{sec}}\]

\[\mathrm{E_{max}=NBA\omega}\]

\[=100\times0.05\times1\times2\pi\]

\[=10\times\pi\]

\[=31.4\,\mathrm{V}\]

questions.question:
The magnetic flux linked to a circular coil of radius R is

\(\phi = 2{t^3} + 4{t^2} + 2t + 5\) Wb

The magnitude of induced emf in the coil at t = 5 s is
questions.explanation:
Given magnetic flux is

\[\phi = 2{t^3} + 4{t^2} + 2t + 5\]

Induced emf is given by

\[\varepsilon = {{ - d\phi } \over {dt}} = {{ - d} \over {dt}}(2{t^3} + 4{t^2} + 2t + 5)\]

\[|\varepsilon | = 6{t^2} + 8t + 2\]

At \(t = 5\) s,

\[|\varepsilon | = 6 \times 25 + 8 \times 5 + 2\]

\[= 150 + 40 + 2\]

\(= 192\) V

questions.question: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 \(\Omega\) is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux (\(\phi\)B) = \(\overrightarrow B\) . \(\overrightarrow A\)

\(\overrightarrow B\) and \(\overrightarrow A\) are in same direction, therefore

\(\phi\)B = B . A = 0.5 \(\times\) 12

= 0.5 Wb

questions.question: Two conducting circular loops of radii R<sub>1</sub> and R<sub>2</sub> are placed in the same plane with their centres coinciding. If R<sub>1</sub> >> R<sub>2</sub>, the mutual inductance M between them will be directly proportional to :
questions.explanation:
Two concentric coils are of radius R1 and R2 as shown


Let current in outer loop be i

Magnetic field at center = B = \({{{\mu _0}i} \over {2{R_1}}}\)

Magnetic flux through inner coil = B \(\times\) \(\pi R_2^2\)

\(\Rightarrow\) \(\phi\) = \({{{\mu _0}i} \over {2{R_1}}} \times \pi R_2^2\)

As per definition, \(\phi\) = Mi

\(\Rightarrow\) M = \(( {{{{\mu _0}\pi } \over 2}} ){{R_2^2} \over {{R_1}}}\)

\(\therefore\) M \(\propto\) \({{R_2^2} \over {{R_1}}}\)

questions.question: A 800 turn coil of effective area 0.05 m<sup>2</sup> is kept.  perpendicular to a magnetic filed 5 × 10<sup>–5</sup> T. When the plane of the coil is rotated by 90<sup>o</sup> around any of its coplanar axis in 0.1 s, the emf induced in the coil will be :
questions.explanation:
Given N = 800, A = 0.05 m2 , B = 5 × 10–5 T

\(\Delta\)t = 0.15 s

We know, e = \(- {{( {{\phi _f} - {\phi _i}} )} \over {\Delta t}}\)

= \(- {{( {0 - NBA} )} \over {\Delta t}}\)

= \({{800 \times 5 \times {{10}^{ - 5}} \times 5 \times {{10}^{ - 2}}} \over {0.1}}\)

= 0.02 V

questions.question: A long solenoid of diameter 0.1 m has 2 \(\times\) 10<sup>4</sup> turns per meter. At the centre of the solenoid, a coil of 100 turns and radius 0.01 m is placed with its axis coinciding with the solenoid axis. The current in the solenoid reduces at a constant rate to 0 A from 4 A in 0.05 s. If the resistance of the coil is 10 \(\pi\)<sup>2</sup> \(\Omega\), the total charge flowing through the coil during this time is

A uniform magnetic field is restricted within a region of rafius r. The magnetic field changes with time at a rate \({{d\overrightarrow B } \over {dt}}\). Loop 1 of radius R > r encloses the region r and loop 2 of radius R is outside the region of magnetic field as shown in the figure. Then the e.m.f. generated is

options.content: zero in loop 1 and zero in loop 2
\(- {{d\overrightarrow B } \over {dt}}\pi {r^2}\) in loop 1 and \(- {{d\overrightarrow B } \over {dt}}\pi {r^2}\) in loop 2
\(- {{d\overrightarrow B } \over {dt}}\pi {R^2}\) in loop 1 and zero in loop 2
\(- {{d\overrightarrow B } \over {dt}}\pi {r^2}\)  in loop 1 and zero in loop 2

questions.explanation:
Emf generated in loop 1,

\({\varepsilon _1} = - {{d\phi } \over {dt}} = - {d \over {dt}}( {BA} ) = - A \times {{dB} \over {dt}}\)

\(\Rightarrow\) \({\varepsilon _1} = - \pi {r^2} \times {{dB} \over {dt}}\)

Emf generated in loop 2,

\({\varepsilon _2} = - {{d\phi } \over {dt}} = - {d \over {dt}}( {BA} ) = - {d \over {dt}}( {0 \times A} )\) = 0

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
A thin semicircular conducting ring (PQR) of radius r is falling with its plane vertical in a horizontal magnetic field B, as shown in the figure.


The potential difference developed across the ring when its speed is \(v\), is

options.content: \({{Bv\pi {r^2}} \over 2}\) and P is at higher potential
\(\pi rBV\) and R is at higher potential
2rBV and R is at higher potential

questions.explanation:
Potential difference that is developed across ring when its speed is v :

\(\varepsilon\) = B v (li – lf)

where, li – lf = displacement between end of semicircular ring = 2r

Hence, \(\varepsilon\) = Bv(2r) where R is at high potential.

questions.question:
A coil of resistance 400 \(\Omega\) is placed in a magnetic field. If the magnetic flux \(\phi\) (Wb) linked with the coil varies with time t (sec) as \(\phi = 50{t^2} + 4\).

The current in the coil at t = 2 sec is

According, to Faraday’s law of induction

Induced e.m.f, \(\varepsilon = - {{d\phi } \over {dt}}\) = -(100t)

Induced current i at t = 2 sec.

= \(| {{\varepsilon \over R}} | = + {{100 \times 2} \over {400}}\) = +0.5 A

questions.question: The current \(i\) in a coil varies with time as shown in the figure. The variation of induced emf with time would be
questions.explanation:
e = -L\({{di} \over {dt}}\)

During 0 to \({T \over 4}\), \({{di} \over {dt}}\) = constant

\(\therefore\) e = -ve

During \({T \over 4}\) to \({T \over 2}\), \({{di} \over {dt}}\) = 0

\(\therefore\) e = 0

During \({T \over 2}\) to \({3T \over 4}\), \({{di} \over {dt}}\) = 0

\(\therefore\) e = +ve

Thus graph given in option (a) represents the variation of induced emf with time.

questions.question: A conducting circular loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field, B = 0.025 T with its plane perpendicular to the loop. The radius of the loop is made to shrink at a constant rate of 1 mm s<sup>\(-\)1</sup>. The induced emf when the radius is 2 cm, is
questions.explanation:
Constant rate at which radius of the loop shrinks

\({{dr} \over {dt}} = 1 \times {10^{-3}}\) m s-1

Magnetic flux linked with the loop is

\(\phi\) = BAcos\(\phi\) = B(\(\pi\)r2)cos0o = B\(\pi\)r2

The magnitude of the induced emf is

|e| = \({{d\phi } \over {dt}} = {d \over {dt}}( {B\pi {r^2}} ) = B\pi 2r{{dr} \over {dt}}\)

= 0.025 \(\times\) \(\pi\) \(\times\) 2 \(\times\) 2 \(\times\) 10-2 \(\times\) 1 \(\times\) 10-3

= \(\pi\) \(\times\) 10-6 V

= \(\pi \mu V\)

questions.question: A conducting circular loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field 0.04 T with its plane perpendicular to the magnetic field. The radius of the loop starts shrinking at 2 mm/s. The induced emf in the loop when the radius is 2 cm is
questions.explanation:
Constant rate at which radius of the loop shrinks

\({{dr} \over {dt}} = 2 \times {10^{-3}}\) m s-1

Magnetic flux linked with the loop is

\(\phi\) = BAcos\(\phi\) = B(\(\pi\)r2)cos0o = B\(\pi\)r2

The magnitude of the induced emf is

|e| = \({{d\phi } \over {dt}} = {d \over {dt}}( {B\pi {r^2}} ) = B\pi 2r{{dr} \over {dt}}\)

= 0.04 \(\times\) \(\pi\) \(\times\) 2 \(\times\) 2 \(\times\) 10-2 \(\times\) 2 \(\times\) 10-3

= 3.2\(\pi\) \(\times\) 10-6 V

questions.question: A circular disc of radius 0.2 meter is placed in a uniform magnetic field of induction \({1 \over \pi }( {{{Wb} \over {{m^2}}}} )\) in such a way that its axis makes an angle of 60<sup>o</sup> with \(\overrightarrow B .\) The magnetic flux linked with the disc is
questions.explanation:
Given B = \({1 \over \pi }( {{{Wb} \over {{m^2}}}} )\)

\(\theta\) = 60o

Area normal to the plane of the disc

= \(\pi\)r2 cos60o = \({{\pi {r^2}} \over 2}\)

Flux = B × normal area

= \({{0.02 \times 0.02} \over 2}\) = 0.02 Wb

questions.question: A long solenoid has 500 turns. When a current of 2 ampere is passed through it, the resulting magnetic flux linked with each turn of the solenoid is 4 \(\times\) 10<sup>\(-\)3</sup> Wb. The self-inductance of the solenoid is
questions.explanation:
Total number of turns in the solenoid,

N = 500 Current, I = 2A.

Magnetic flux linked with each turn = 4 × 10–3 Wb

Self inductance of coil :

L = \({{N\phi } \over I} = {{500 \times 4 \times {{10}^3}} \over 2}\) = 1 H

questions.question: Two coils of self inductance 2 mH and 8 mH are placed so close together that the effective flux in one coil is completely linked with the other. The mutual inductance between these coils is
questions.explanation:
Mutual inductance is given as,

M = K\(\sqrt {{L_1} \times {L_2}}\)

Now given, K = 1, L1 = 2 mH, L2 = 8 mH

\(\therefore\) M = \(1 \times \sqrt {2 \times 8}\) = 4 mH

questions.explanation:

\(\Rightarrow\) \({\Delta \phi = ( {i\Delta t} )R}\) = QR

\(\Rightarrow\) Q = \({{\Delta \phi } \over R}\)

questions.question: For a coil having L = 2 mH, current flow through it is \(I = {t^2}{e^{ - t}}\) then, the time at which emf become zero
questions.explanation:
Given, \(I = {t^2}{e^{ - t}}\)

So, \({{dI} \over {dt}} = 2t{e^{ - t}} - {t^2}{e^{ - t}}\)

\(| \varepsilon | = L{{dI} \over {dt}}\)

here emf is zero when \({{dI} \over {dt}}\) = 0

\(\therefore\) \(2t{e^{ - t}} - {t^2}{e^{ - t}}\) = 0

\(\Rightarrow\) \(2t{e^{ - t}} = {t^2}{e^{ - t}}\)

\(\Rightarrow\) \(t{e^{ - t}}( {t - 2} )\) = 0

As t \(\ne\) \(\infty\), t \(\ne\) 0

\(\therefore\) t = 2 sec
